requirements.text: Make her close her jacket fully

outcomes.description: The woman's jacket is closed completely.
outcomes.target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.
outcomes.reference: The woman's jacket in the input image.

nodes.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed, with its actual front closure edges joined throughout and no remaining front opening?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence establishes that the jacket's actual front closure edges are joined throughout the full closure and no opening remains. Fail when an identifiable opening between those edges remains at any section, even if another section is visibly closed. Compare corresponding closure-edge features across the source and edited images; distinguish the actual closure from the outer silhouette, projecting pink fabric, folds, sleeves, and bottom hem. Neither a broad pink flap nor the absence of a visible gap establishes full closure when the closure is concealed. Unknown when the closure cannot be located or traced sufficiently to establish completion, and no identifiable remaining opening establishes failure. A visible closed portion alone is insufficient for pass.
nodes.binding: Reference garment: the woman's pink jacket in the SOURCE image. Locate its front panel edges on either side of the visible dark central strip, following them from the neckline toward the lower front hem; the strip identifies the opening region but is not itself a fastener. Evaluation target: the corresponding front closure of that same jacket in the EDITED image. Account for the changed sideways pose: first locate the neckline below her head, distinguish the sleeve containing the visible hand from the torso panels, and locate the torso panel's lower hem above or alongside the dark trousers. Use these landmarks to search for the corresponding front edges from neckline to lower front hem, inspecting upper, middle, and lower portions without treating them as separate requirements. The large pink section projecting toward image-right is not by itself evidence of either closure or an opening; identify its relationship to the actual front edges before using it as evidence. Do not substitute a sleeve boundary, side seam, fold, outer contour, or bottom hem for the closure. Requested state: the actual front edges meet throughout, leaving no front opening. If any identifiable section remains open, fail; if no opening is identifiable but any necessary section remains concealed or untraceable, retain unknown rather than infer full closure.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The unresolved result is explicitly a transport failure, not negative visual evidence; do not alter the visual criterion to compensate for it. The binding is already detailed, but its source-specific landmarks may be brittle under pose changes. Keep the same-jacket correspondence and full-closure standard, while directing the evaluator to inspect the edited image’s visible torso/front edges and distinguish them from the projecting pink panel, sleeve, folds, and silhouette. Preserve unknown when the actual closure cannot be traced; fail only on an identifiable remaining opening and pass only with evidence that the closure meets throughout. Improve execution reliability through the evaluation pipeline’s retry/fallback handling rather than weakening or changing the node’s requirements.
